name: Rice beverages (rice milk)

Pb.control: Confirmed no-ML (standards-no-ml-confirmed.csv): no government sets a lead ML specific to rice-based drinks; the EU 2023/915 beverage lead framework does not enumerate a rice-drink row. Lead is material in a rice-derived beverage but unregulated by ML; literature-baseline governs. iAs is the binding Tier-1 analyte for this subcategory.
Pb.reference_method: Pb by ICP-MS on the as-consumed liquid.

tAs.control: No government sets a total-arsenic ML for a rice-based beverage in any jurisdiction; the binding arsenic control for this subcategory is the inorganic-arsenic ML (30 ug/kg, EU 2023/915 non-alcoholic rice drinks). A dry "rice and derivatives" total-arsenic ceiling is not comparable at face value to a dilute as-consumed beverage, and total arsenic adds no ceiling beyond the inorganic-arsenic limit here.
tAs.reference_method: tAs by ICP-MS on the as-consumed liquid; speciate to iAs on any elevated total-arsenic result.

tHg.control: Mercury does not accumulate in a rice-derived beverage; the only cereal mercury MLs are dry-basis and no government sets a rice-drink mercury ML. Not a material contaminant in this matrix.

MeHg.control: No government sets a methylmercury ML for a rice-based beverage in any jurisdiction; methylmercury maximum levels exist only for fish and seafood. Mercury does not accumulate in a rice-derived beverage and is not a material contaminant in this matrix.

Cd.control: Confirmed no-ML (standards-no-ml-confirmed.csv): no government sets a cadmium ML specific to rice-based drinks. Material but unregulated by ML; literature-baseline governs.
Cd.reference_method: Cd by ICP-MS on the as-consumed liquid.

Cr.control: No jurisdiction sets a total-chromium maximum level for a rice-derived beverage; the grain total-Cr limits (China GB 2762-2022, 1.0 mg/kg) are dry-grain basis and do not read across to an as-consumed liquid. Reflex total-Cr screen on the liquid.
Cr.reference_method: Total-Cr by ICP-MS on the as-consumed liquid; no sovereign rice-beverage total-Cr ML.

Cr-VI.control: Cr(VI) (hexavalent chromium): reflex-speciation control on the total-chromium result (see the separate total-Cr cell, governed by China GB 2762-2022 grains/milled-grain-products total Cr 1.0 mg/kg). No jurisdiction sets a Cr(VI)-specific food maximum level; chromium in the as-consumed rice-beverage liquid is dominated by nutritionally-essential Cr(III) and any Cr(VI) reduces to Cr(III) in the matrix. Reflex control: any total-Cr result >= 100 ug/kg triggers Cr(VI) speciation, and any quantifiable Cr(VI) fails.
Cr-VI.reference_method: Total-Cr screen by ICP-MS; on any result >= 100 ug/kg, Cr(VI) by EN 15192 / EPA 6800 IC-ICP-MS isotope-dilution; LOQ-level quantifiable Cr(VI) = fail.

Ni.control: The EU 2024/1987 nickel MLs are scoped to cereal grains as commodities and to juices/nectars, not to a rice-based drink; no government sets a rice-drink nickel ML. Not a binding cell.

Sn.control: Canned-only analyte; carton-packed rice milk is not tinplate-packaged.

Al.control: No credible regulator sets an aluminium CONTAMINANT maximum level for grains, cereals, or rice products, and China GB 2762 (the contaminant standard) does not regulate aluminium. Aluminium present in leavened, baked, or alum-firmed grain products is permitted-additive residue (China GB 2760-2024 food-additive use limits, e.g. baked foods 100 mg/kg / starch noodles and vermicelli 200 mg/kg, calculated as Al), governed by additive ADI and the JECFA/EFSA provisional tolerable weekly intake, not by a per-food contaminant ML. An additive-use residue cap is not a contaminant government limit and is not published as one; background aluminium in plain grain is soil-derived. Managed by intake vs the TWI, not a lookup.
Al.reference_method: Managed by intake vs JECFA/EFSA TWI; periodic total-Al screen (ICP-MS); no per-food contaminant ML to look up.

method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default, 8:1 basis, read-across)
